name: J Kenneth Salisbury, Jr.
title: Professor (Research) of Computer Science and of Surgery (Anatomy), Emeritus
department: Computer Science (also Surgery (Anatomy); courtesy appointment in Mechanical Engineering per lab page)
research_topics: roller graspers with steerable rolling fingertips
camera-based tactile sensing inside compliant rollers
closed-loop grasp force control and object shape reconstruction
vibratory / impact-driven part transport in grippers
haptic device design and haptic rendering
current_direction: Tactile-reactive roller graspers with cameras inside the rollers
Continuous rolling contact instead of discontinuous finger-gaiting
In-hand 6-DoF manipulation with closed-loop grasp force control
Hybrid rolling-fingertip + finger-gaiting manipulation as the stated next step
current_direction_basis: Driven almost entirely by evidence item 1, the 2025 IEEE T-RO paper 'Tactile-Reactive Roller Grasper' (DOI 10.1109/TRO.2025.3543324), whose fetched OpenAlex abstract states the design 'uses image processing from cameras placed inside steerable compliant rollers to track contact conditions and locations', that the same data is used 'to reconstruct object shape', that converting in-hand manipulation 'from a discontinuous process ... to a continuous process' yields a convergent control loop, and that 'hybrid rolling fingertip and finger-gaiting approaches to manipulation may be a promising future research direction' -- that last sentence is the source of the fifth phrase. Reinforced by evidence item 2 (Roller Grasper V3, IEEE T-RO 2024, full 6-DoF SE(3) in-hand manipulation), evidence item 3 (ICRA 2024 vibratory transport of grasped parts, which is the same mechanism-design-for-manipulation thread), and evidence item 5 (the lab's 'Grasper Design' project page, last modified 2024-08-07, which groups Tactile-Reactive Roller Grasper, Roller Grasper V3/V2/V1 and Curling Gripper as the current project family). Deliberately NOT based on the CS/Profiles biography, which still describes older work (PHANToM, da Vinci, PR-2, surgical simulation) and has not been rewritten to reflect the roller-grasper line.

evidence.title: Tactile-Reactive Roller Grasper
evidence.summary: IEEE Transactions on Robotics, 2025, vol. 41, pp. 1938-1955. Authors: Shenli Yuan, Shaoxiong Wang, Radhen Patel, Megha Tippur, Connor L. Yako, Mark R. Cutkosky, Edward H. Adelson, Kenneth Salisbury (Stanford + MIT). Fetched abstract: roller graspers with steerable rolling fingertips achieve 'six degree of freedom mobility and closed-loop grasp force control'; the design 'uses image processing from cameras placed inside steerable compliant rollers to track contact conditions and locations', the same data reconstructs object shape, and continuous rolling replaces discontinuous finger-gaiting to give a convergent control loop. This is the single most recent research output found for him. Confirmed independently on OpenAlex and on his Stanford Profiles publication list.

evidence.title: Design and Control of Roller Grasper V3 for In-Hand Manipulation
evidence.summary: IEEE Transactions on Robotics, 2024, vol. 40, pp. 4222-4234. Authors: Shenli Yuan, Lin Shao, Yunhai Feng, Jiatong Sun, Teng Xue, Connor L. Yako, Jeannette Bohg, J. Kenneth Salisbury. Fetched abstract: a 'nonanthropomorphic robot grasper with a steerable roller on each of its four fingertips' plus a manipulation architecture (high-level waypoint planner + low-level control policy) achieving 'full 6-DoF manipulation of the grasped object in SE(3)'. Co-authored with Jeannette Bohg, indicating an active tie to Stanford's learning-based robotics group.

evidence.title: Vertical Vibratory Transport of Grasped Parts Using Impacts
evidence.summary: IEEE ICRA 2024 (venue inferred from the DOI string 10.1109/ICRA57147.2024.10610769; OpenAlex returned a null source name for this record, so the venue is not independently confirmed by a fetched venue field). Authors: Connor L. Yako, J. Nowak, Shenli Yuan, Kenneth Salisbury -- i.e. led by the lab's current PhD student. Fetched abstract: uses 'impact-induced acceleration in conjunction with periodic stick-slip to successfully and quickly transport parts vertically against gravity', validated with a flexure/voice-coil vibrating surface fitted to a parallel-jaw gripper.
evidence.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2024 -- inferred from DOI, not from a fetched venue field

state_rationale: No formal opening exists: an exhaustive text search of all 76 pages and 6 posts of sr.stanford.edu found no join / openings / prospective-students / recruiting statement of any kind, so this cannot be OPENING. It is above WATCH because there is genuine recent evidence: a 2025 IEEE Transactions on Robotics paper with him as senior author (Tactile-Reactive Roller Grasper), a 2024 T-RO paper and a 2024 ICRA paper, a current PhD student (Connor Yako) who is first author on the ICRA 2024 paper, lab project pages refreshed 2024-08-07, and a current-academic-year (2025-26) Stanford Profiles listing for CS 199 Independent Work and CS 191/191W Senior Project. A direct, personal email address for him appears on his own lab page, which makes a cold email actually deliverable. Two caveats a student must weigh: (1) he is Emeritus, and the group is small -- one current PhD student listed -- so capacity is likely very limited; (2) no undergraduate has been listed as a lab member since roughly 2013-2021, and the lab's news feed has been dead since 2013. A cold email is reasonable and low-cost, but expectations should be calibrated to an emeritus PI running a small, quiet group rather than an actively recruiting lab.
